encounter_greeting.text: Halt, traveller, and hear the banner of Lauresse before you draw steel. I am {persona}, sworn to Corbanel, and I have not forgotten the fen raiders who burned my family's hall.
Good day, ser {player}. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, riding the causeways as my grandsire swore I should. Let us see whether your road and mine run together.
Ser {player}, my heart lifts to see you upon this road. Tell me your business, for I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and I would gladly share bread and tale with you.
You stand in the path of {my_faction}, ser {player}. Yield the road or prove your mettle, for {persona} will chronicle whichever you choose.

encounter_threatened.text: You would have {gold} from me? Then you must first pry it from my cold hands, ser {player}. Lauresse does not pay tribute to threats.
Ser {player}, a demand of {gold} is a bold word for a stranger on the causeway. Speak more plainly, and I shall answer as my oath requires.
Threaten me for {gold} and you shall have a tale worth telling, ser {player}. My grandsire fought worse men than you on the causeways of Corbanel.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, for no friend of mine would name a price of {gold} with such a face. Let us speak of honour instead.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: I accept, ser {player}, and gladly. Let our banners stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let the minstrels sing of this day.
Very well, ser {player}. An oath is sworn between us, and I shall keep mine to the last. Do not ask me to forgive {rival}, however.
By the honour of Lauresse, I take your hand, ser {player}. Together we shall break {enemy_faction}, and I will remember the service you do me.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. A banner of Lauresse does not march beside a stranger who has not earned its trust. Go and earn it, if you can.
I must decline, ser {player}. My oath is sworn to Corbanel alone, and I will not bind it to any road I have not walked.
I am grieved to refuse you, ser {player}, truly. Yet while {rival} still rides these causeways, I dare not promise what I cannot keep.
Propose an alliance to me? Ask {rival} to kneel first, ser {player}, and then we shall speak of oaths.

captured_by_player.text: Your blade has bested mine, ser {player}, and I stand as your captive. Name your ransom of {gold}, and know that {my_faction} will remember this humbling.
So the causeways have bound me. Very well, ser {player}, you have won this field, and I shall bear my captivity with what dignity remains to me.
A fair fight, ser {player}, and well fought. I am your prisoner now, and I would rather lose to you than to any fen raider. Name your terms.
Bind me, then, and be quick about it! The banner of Lauresse does not weep in chains, though {my_faction} shall surely pay {gold} to see me free.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me go without a ransom. I shall remember that mercy longer than any blade you ever raised.
Ser {player} has loosed me from chains without ransom. A rare grace on these causeways, and I will not forget it.
You spared me, ser {player}, but do not think this humbles me. Lauresse pays its debts, and this one I shall repay in steel.
Honour to ser {player}, who freed me without gold. The chronicle of Lauresse shall record it under mercy, not under ransom.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has forsaken {my_faction} for {faction} like a coward slinking off the field. Let the minstrels mock the deserter.
You turned your banner to {faction}, ser {player}, and {my_faction} is poorer for it. An oath broken is a stain no ballad will wash clean.
Ser {player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Such roads are open to all, yet honour does not travel as lightly as a rider does.
I bear you no grudge, ser {player}, though I grieve that your oath to {my_faction} is broken. May {faction} prove worthy of you.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has drawn sword against {enemy_faction}. The banner of Lauresse rides to war, and the fen raiders shall not sleep easy tonight.
Hear, all Ormerath: {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are at war. Lauresse keeps its oath, and blood shall answer each lost hall.
Word has come that {enemy_faction} stands against {my_faction}. I ride to the causeways gladly, for my grandsire's oath demands it.
War between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}! Let each honest blade sharpen its edge, for the chronicle of Lauresse is not yet finished.

fought_alongside_player.text: {troop_count} of the enemy fell today against {enemy_faction}, and ser {player} stood at my side like a true knight. Sing it!
Ser {player}, that charge against {enemy_faction} was glorious. With {troop_count} of ours behind you, we broke their line. My thanks, friend.
Well struck, ser {player}. We bore {troop_count} men against {enemy_faction}, and the field is ours. I have no doubt the chroniclers will name this day rightly.
A hard-won field against {enemy_faction}, ser {player}, with {troop_count} of our number left standing. Honour enough for one day.

encounter_farewell.text: Fare you well, ser {player}. May your road be smooth and your oaths be kept, and should we meet again, I shall greet you with a full heart.
Until we cross paths again, ser {player}. Our roads part here, and I shall ride on with the banner held high.
Go, then, ser {player}, and count yourself lucky to leave with your purse. The next meeting shall be settled with steel, not courtesy.
Begone from my sight, ser {player}. I have marked your face and your name, and neither shall slip from my memory.

ambient_chatter.text: Mist lies thick over {village} this morning and the causeways run slick with dew. A poor day to ride, yet honour waits for no sunshine.
Ale at {town} tastes of home tonight, friends. I raise my cup to every rider who keeps faith on the long roads.
My grandsire crossed these marshes in a storm worse than this. Such weather tests a banner, and Lauresse has never lowered its own.
Pellegrane's towers were grey as slate when I rode past, and yet they stood. So too shall we, friends, if we hold firm.
Fen raiders have been seen near {village}. Keep your watch sharp and your blades ready, for I have seen what they leave behind.
